- When sentiment is consistently low or negative, model tends to underpredict prices; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% to compensate for bearish sentiment bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overreacts and forecasts a prolonged overshoot; reduce forecast peak by 3–5% and apply early mean reversion.
- If recent history shows strong upward momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive rising prices), model frequently overestimates continuation; cap forecast growth at 2–3% above prior peak.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed, model often fails to capture mean reversion; add a 1–2% downward bias in the 5–10 day horizon to reflect volatility decay.
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently underestimates true price at the end of the horizon; apply a 1–3% upward adjustment to final 5–7 days to account for lagged momentum.
- If sentiment history shows increasing bullishness (e.g., >0.50 for 3+ days), model tends to overforecast; reduce forecast by 1–2% for the next 3–5 days to avoid overcorrection.
